MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 14, 2025
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Ruesch at 5:00 p.m., on January 14, 2025, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on January 9,2025, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Ruesch

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Elaine Lister, City Manager
  Jerry Hill, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

RECESS AND RECONVENE MEETING

At the hour of 5:00 pm Mayor Ruesch recessed the meeting. Mayor Ruesch reconvened the
meeting at 6:00 pm with all five City Council Members present.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Ruesch

Mayor Ruesch asked for an update on Emergency Response

City Council Minutes  1  January 14, 2025
 Chief of Police Ivins, Fire Chief Cheyne Maule gave update on emergency preparedness. Saundra
Jacobs and Frank Ury of Santa Margarita Water District gave update on water supply. Emergency
Operations Manager Paul Catsimanes also gave an update on the city’s response to the high winds.

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Presentation to Former Mayor Trish Kelley

  Mayor Ruesch presented former Mayor Kelley the gavel plaque.

P2. Opening Remarks from Mayor Bob Ruesch

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Jeff McBride, M.V.: Spoke on the dangerous intersection signal timing at Felipe and Oso Parkway
and pointed out that Lake Mission Viejo is a dead lake due to the change to reclaimed water.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: Voiced his argument on the unwritten rotation policy of the Mayor and Mayor
Pro Tem. He spoke on his objection to Council Member Vasquez being blackballed as Mayor Pro
Tem this year.

Andrea Richard, M.V.: Asked for more police presence in the parking lot at Los Alisos Middle
School for the revving of cars late at night. She stated she has called the non-emergency line, and
nothing has been done.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Spoke on her records request as to why Measure Y documentation was
removed from City Hall and was told that it was attorney-client communications. He then outlined
her email exchanges with City Attorney Bill Curley.

Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Spoke on the need for mixed-use housing across the street and asked the
Council to keep an open mind.

Robert Breton, M.V.: Congratulated the City Council on a new year. He outlined the differences
between incompetent leaders within our State and our local government who have protected our
city from disasters and that their priorities are properly placed.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

20. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell asked the City Manager for an update regarding the public comment
received this evening on the intersection of Oso Parkway and Felipe. City Manager Elaine Lister
stated the project to widen the entire intersection is in the final design stage and they hope to be in
construction within the next year and she does understand the urgency and will see if this project
can be moved up. The project, when completed will provide dual left turn lanes in all directions.
Council Member Goodell did comment that he has been rear-ended at this intersection with one of
his sons in the car many years ago. He stated that he did attend the 20th Anniversary of Bathgate
Elementary School and reminded residents of the original principal Curt Visca who had a show on
Cox Cable called Curtoon Time that taught children how to draw. He said it was fun to see him
and reminisce.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley congratulate Sherry Merryfield on being named Employee of the Year.
She also recognized Emergency Operations Manager Paul Catsimanes for all his work the past two
weeks with updating the Council on the winds and fire news, as well as Community Relations
Director Robert Schick. She commented on outstanding work Public Services has made with
cleaning up the mess from the winds and gave kudos to Jerry Hill and staff. Council Member
Kelley also thanked residents for their generous participation in the Christmas gift drive for our
Marine Adoption Committee and mentioned that there are left over gifts that will be given out at
the Marines Mission Viejo Lake Day. She gave a shoutout to Castille Elementary School for being
recognized in U.S. News and World Report Best Elementary School Rankings. They are the
number one elementary school in Capo Unified School District and ranked 17th out of 47 of Orange
County’s best elementary schools along with being a high achiever in California ranked 165 out
of 5,857 schools. Council Member Kelley attended the following events: Animal Shelter
Volunteer Holiday Party; Grand Opening of Cookie Plug; Whoville Night Market; and the Holiday
Mix and Mingle. She thanked staff for all their hard work. She also attended the Jewish Festival
of Lights at the Norman P. Murray Community Center; a ribbon cutting at Laguna Wellness and
Weight Loss on Alicia Parkway; Bathgate Elementary School 30th Anniversary; and the Orange
County Division of the League of California Cities meeting

Council Member Vasquez

City Council Minutes  9  January 14, 2025
 Council Member Vasquez attended the Animal Shelter Volunteer Holiday Party and commented
what an impressive group of volunteers and that it really takes a special person to provide the love
and care for animals. She stated that she really appreciates what these volunteers do. She also
attended the Jane Austen Ball at the Library and won a basket with Jane Austen books. Council
Member Vasquez also attended the Night Market and commented on the great turnout. She
attended the Festival of Lights and is looking forward to seeing how much the attendance grows
this year. Lastly, she gave a recap on her daughter’s girl scout troop that participated in a
community service project at Ivey Park Senior Living. She announced that Girl Scout Cookie
Season is here. Lastly, she congratulated Sherry Merrifield on being named Employee of the Year
and Bathgate Elementary School on their 30th Anniversary.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum also attended the Jane Austen Ball and the Night Market. She
commented that a couple of the shops across the street stayed open during the night market and
they were busy. In reference to a public comment earlier regarding the status of the store fronts
across the street, Council Member Bucknum commented that those that are there running business
are benefiting from what the city is doing with the night markets. She pointed out a new boutique
next to Delize’s Restaurant with unique items and she recommended residents to visit. Council
Member Bucknum stated our priorities are public safety which include our police and fire and
everything that goes along with supporting them. She stated that we have to keep the pressure on
streamlining and keeping government focused in light of the recent disasters which our insurance
rates will greatly be impacted by what happened in Los Angeles. She is happy to serve on the new
committee addressing property insurance because there needs to be a loud voice. Council Member
Bucknum reminded residents to think about their yards right now with brush, eucalyptus and palm
trees which are highly flammable. She stated that the city does have programs if assistance is
needed and to contact the city. She commented on the charitable donations that were collected at
the farmers market this past Saturday was overwhelming and phenomenal. Lastly, she said it is
going to be a game changer on what happens with the housing and infrastructure in Los Angeles,
and she prays for the best. She wished everyone a Happy New Year.

Mayor Ruesch

Mayor Ruesch announced that we lost firefighter Kevin Skinner due to a medical emergency in
the line of duty. He stated he was honored to attend with Station 24 to honor him on his last ride
home on the overpass of Oso Parkway and expressed that if was very emotional to stand with his
fellow firefighters. He let Council Member Kelley know that Anne Figueroa for Representative
Kate Sanchez was unable to make the meeting this evening but will have something for her
tomorrow.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:46 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Ruesch adjourned the meeting in memory of those who have suffered and perished in the
wildfires in Los Angeles, and resident Patricia Mae Ohman, to Tuesday, January 28, 2025, at 5:00
p.m.
